label: Shared-blind local check flag
definition: noFlag F n is the event that no local check raised a flag: for every index i, the i-th local coordinate lies outside the flag event F. Flags are events on local coordinates only, so a check is blind to the shared coordinate by construction. Conditioning the profile on noFlag represents retaining the assertions after the checks found nothing; it is a probabilistic update, not a guarantee that the remaining assertions are true.
note: Analyst model of the owner's 'foreign word in a coherent sentence' observation for #1584: a local error that conflicts with surrounding structure can be flagged by a local check, while an error in the shared structure itself raises no local conflict. Whether actual corpus cross-checks resemble a discriminating flag is an OPEN application question; see docs/notes/preface-connectivity-1584.md.
